reader.requirement: At --std 85 an indexed REWRITE written with END-REWRITE must end at that terminator: statements after it are outside the INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases; with same-verb nesting each END-REWRITE ends the most recent unterminated REWRITE (§1985:IV.6.4.3), with or without conditional phrases on it; without the terminator the phrase runs to the period or to the containing statement's next phrase; a terminator with no REWRITE to end is refused. The witnesses cover the 1985 format and the FROM operand, not the scope.

edition-consulted.switches: a phrase associates only with a format available at the edition (ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable on the format's construct); REWRITE's one format, Pair(InvalidKey), carries no construct, so 85 and 2023 take the same arm
gates REWRITE FILE and the RECORD word after record-name (2002 on), and the retry/lock phrases, at 85; END-REWRITE is not gated

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the scope; the 1985 REWRITE format lacks FILE file-name, RECORD, the lock and retry phrases, which are refused at 85 by the version-conformance pass
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise the 1985 format and FROM operand; the terminator's scope, nesting of REWRITE within REWRITE and the refusal of a stray END-REWRITE are not exercised

reader.notes: END-REWRITE is an optional token closing the rewriteStatement rule, and the one conditionalPhrases predicate assigns each INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY to the nearest unterminated statement that may take it, so the terminator's scope falls out of the parse at every edition. A run of six scope shapes and four refusals matched the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR11 and the scope text it points to (§1985:IV.6.4.3, §1985:IV.4.4.4 item 2). Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-01/: r3-nest2 (P1: a delimited REWRITE inside a failing READ's INVALID KEY, then a statement and NOT INVALID KEY: prints 'P1 READ INVALID / P1 RW INVALID / P1 IN READ PHRASE', so NOT INVALID KEY went to READ; P2 READ succeeds: only 'P2 READ NOT INVALID', REWRITE skipped; P4 ELSE implicitly ends an unterminated REWRITE: 'P4 RW INVALID / P4 IN PHRASE / P4 AFTER'; P5 delimited REWRITE inside inline PERFORM twice) all as the text says; --std 2023 output identical (md5). r3-nest (no END-REWRITE inside READ INVALID KEY) and r3-condinimp (unterminated REWRITE inside another REWRITE's INVALID KEY) refused COBOL2796: correct, the 1985 phrase operand is imperative-statement-1 and only a delimited scope statement is imperative. r3-seq (class e, ACCESS SEQUENTIAL): REWRITE with no prior READ 'DECL 43 / E1 AFTER 43' (neither phrase runs, statement after END-REWRITE does); changed prime key 'E2 INVALID 21 / E2 AFTER'; REWRITE on a closed file 'DECL 49 / E3 AFTER 49'. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR11; OK §1985:IV.6.4.3; OK §1985:IV.4.4.4 (GR2).
